title: Risk management officer
description:
Confira a vaga para Risk management officer em novo hamburgo. Veja os detalhes e como se candidatar.

About Us  Established in March 2018, Bybit is one of the fastest growing cryptocurrency derivatives exchanges, with more than 70 million registered users. We offer a professional platform where crypto traders can find an ultra-fast matching engine, excellent customer service and multilingual community support. We provide innovative online spot and derivatives trading services, mining and staking products, as well as API support, to retail and institutional clients around the world, and strive to be the most reliable exchange for the emerging digital asset class.  Our core values define us. We listen, care, and improve to create a faster, fairer, and more humane trading environment for our users. Our innovative, highly advanced, user-friendly platform has been designed from the ground-up using best-in-class infrastructure to provide our users with the industry's safest, fastest, fairest, and most transparent trading experience. Built on customer-centric values, we endeavour to provide a professional, 24/7 multi-language customer support to help in a timely manner.  As of today, Bybit is one of the most trusted, reliable, and transparent cryptocurrency derivatives platforms in the space.  Key Responsibilities:   Implement and maintain a comprehensive risk management framework, covering credit, market, liquidity, operational, and technology risks.  Conduct prudential and capital risk assessments, including stress testing, scenario analysis, and capital adequacy evaluations.  Prepare and support regulatory disclosures required for virtual asset service providers (VASPs) and financial institutions.  Oversee Margin-Account Operations, including;  Development of policies governing margin lending and virtual asset collateral  Setting and reviewing maximum loan-to-value (LTV) ratios and haircut levels  Monitoring collateral valuation, capital add-ons and counterparty exposures  Ensuring compliance with client/institutional limits and capital requirements  Net-worth monitoring;  Review and monitor risk indicators across business functions, escalating material breaches or deviations to senior management and the Board.  Maintain independence from commercial and trading lines while ensuring collaboration with Compliance, Finance, and Operations.  Liaise with internal and external auditors, regulators, and governance committees on risk management and capital matters.  Support a risk-aware culture through training, communication, and continuous improvement of risk methodologies.  Deep practical knowledge in CMN Res. 4557/17 regarding the risk management structure, the financial structure and the information disclosure policy management.    Requirements:   Legally resident in Brazil.  Senior-level experience (minimum 7 years) in financial or prudential risk management, preferably within financial institutions, fintechs, or crypto/virtual asset firms.  Demonstrated  independence from commercial functions  and ability to operate as a second-line or independent control function.   Strong knowledge of  Central Bank of Brazil  risk management regulations, capital adequacy standards, and VASP disclosure requirements.   Expertise in market and liquidity risk frameworks, stress testing, and margin-account operations involving virtual assets.  Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Economics, Risk Management, or related field; postgraduate qualification preferred.  Strong quantitative, analytical, and communication skills; fluency in  Portuguese and English  .   Must meet  fit and proper  standards with  no disqualifying factors  , including:   not to have been declared bankrupt or insolvent;  unblemished reputation;  knowledge of the line of business, the services to be provided and the crypto segment, as well as crypto market dynamics and the risks associated with those activities;  technical capability, compatible with the functions to be exercised.  not having been previously rejected or investigated by the Central Bank of Brazil within the past three years for submitting false, omitted, or inconsistent information in any authorization request

title: Landholder and reforestation delivery manager
description:
Empresa está contratando Landholder and reforestation delivery manager em flores da cunha. Confira requisitos e envie seu currículo.

About Nature Co  Nature Co delivers nature-based solutions (Nb S) for investors, corporates and other purpose driven organisations to scale up action on climate change and biodiversity loss. We specialise in nature-based project development including reforestation, agroforestry, farmer managed natural regeneration and mangrove restoration. Nature Co has extensive expertise in working with local communities to protect and restore natural ecosystems through participation in the global voluntary carbon market.  Nature Co is currently implementing a large-scale reforestation project in Brazil for the generation of verified carbon credits.  We are a diverse, mission-driven team that values inclusion, integrity, and innovation. Nature Co is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer, committed to building an equitable and inclusive workplace for all.     Role and responsibilities   The Landholder and Reforestation Delivery Manager is the primary field-based interface with landholders, communities, reforestation contractors, and other local stakeholders for Nature Co’s projects in Brazil. This position will build and manage a pipeline of landholders interested in reforestation, lead outreach and onboarding, coordinate site inspections, lead the collection of relevant data required for carbon standard checks, and lead signature of landholder agreements. The role will also play a key role in ensuring compliance (contracts and carbon standards) as well as coordinate schedules between landholders and contractors for the implementation of reforestation activities. This will include confirming site readiness, conducting periodic field quality audits, documenting and tracking progress, and resolving issues that could delay delivery or degrade quality.  The role requires a strong combination stakeholder engagement and management experience, and a commitment to quality and impact. The role requires extensive travel and field work across Minas Gerais, Bahia and Espírito Santo.  Primary roles and responsibilities include:   Landholder engagement, onboarding, and pipeline management   Map priority municipalities and referral partner networks (city governments, co-ops, farmer associations, NGOs); plan and run outreach activities, events and information sessions.  Manage the landholder onboarding process (identify → qualify → onboard → contract), using CRM/trackers to keep status, documents and next actions current.  Prepare clear information packs (benefits, obligations, timelines) and respond to inquiries in a timely, professional manner.  Maintain ongoing landholder relationship management to support retention, satisfaction, and smooth site access throughout implementation.    Eligibility, due diligence & agreements   Coordinate site inspections and initial diagnostics in consultation with other team members (parcel boundaries, vegetation status, access, water, risks).  Support land tenure verification and FPIC documentation  Lead closure of contract signatures.  Maintain organized repository of all landholder records within Nature Co’s data management system   (land titles, eligibility documents, contracts, site maps, inspection notes, photos, consultation records).  Reforestation delivery enablement   Translate signed landholder agreements into implementation-ready site plans (site-specific scope, access instructions, constraints, schedule windows).  Align field schedules with landholders and contractors to ensure access, minimize disruption to farm activities, and maintain trust and cooperation.  Support in the delivery of field delivery progress from contractors by site (start/finish dates, activities completed, challenges, next steps), and escalate issues early (access, weather delays, input shortages, labor constraints).  Support in monitoring reforestation activities (during and post planting) and coordinate, where required, rapid response with contractors/landholders (grazing, fire risk, pests, drought stress).    Stakeholder engagement and safeguards   Plan and document stakeholder consultations and community meetings in accordance with Nature Co policies and procedures (agendas, attendance lists, minutes, photos).  Support the team in the operation of the grievance mechanism: receiving grievances and responding in accordance with the Nature Co grievance mechanism.  Maintain landholder contact and ensure landholder information is kept up to date.  Coordinate access, for other project staff and contractors as required.    Reporting   Lead or assist the development of formal monthly, quarterly, and annual project implementation reports for internal and external stakeholders in line with contract and/or carbon standard requirements.  Prepare ad hoc reports, documents, and presentations for internal and external stakeholders.    Teamwork and culture   Support the management of a cross-functional, international team, fostering collaboration and ensuring that project milestones and goals are met.  Stay current on emerging best practices in Nb S and carbon projects; proactively share insights across the organisation and with partners.    Skills and attributes   To perform successfully in this role, you will have:  A minimum of five (5) years of experience in reforestation projects with direct contact with rural landholders and reforestation planting service providers.  Degree in forest engineering, agronomy, ecology, or environmental science.  Intermediate English and native Portuguese language skills  Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to engage confidently across cultures and stakeholder groups.  Strong project management skills, including experience managing timelines, deliverables, and working across multidisciplinary teams.  A proactive, self-starting approach with the ability to anticipate problems, adapt quickly, and take initiative under limited supervision.  A collaborative mindset and ability to lead and motivate internal teams and external partners  Ability to provide strategic and technical guidance across complex, multi-stakeholder projects.  Strong organisational skills and attention to detail in documentation and reporting.  A positive, energetic personality with resilience and drive to see projects through to delivery.    Extensive travel within Brazil is a requirement to perform this position.   Location    Remote, with residence in Minas Gerais, Espirito Santo, or Bahia    Submission instructions   Email CV and brief cover letter to with subject: Landholder and Reforestation Delivery Manager  Submission deadline: 30 March 2026

title: Landholder and reforestation delivery manager
description:
Empresa está contratando Landholder and reforestation delivery manager em são josé dos pinhais. Confira requisitos e envie seu currículo.

About Nature Co  Nature Co delivers nature-based solutions (Nb S) for investors, corporates and other purpose driven organisations to scale up action on climate change and biodiversity loss. We specialise in nature-based project development including reforestation, agroforestry, farmer managed natural regeneration and mangrove restoration. Nature Co has extensive expertise in working with local communities to protect and restore natural ecosystems through participation in the global voluntary carbon market.  Nature Co is currently implementing a large-scale reforestation project in Brazil for the generation of verified carbon credits.  We are a diverse, mission-driven team that values inclusion, integrity, and innovation. Nature Co is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer, committed to building an equitable and inclusive workplace for all.     Role and responsibilities   The Landholder and Reforestation Delivery Manager is the primary field-based interface with landholders, communities, reforestation contractors, and other local stakeholders for Nature Co’s projects in Brazil. This position will build and manage a pipeline of landholders interested in reforestation, lead outreach and onboarding, coordinate site inspections, lead the collection of relevant data required for carbon standard checks, and lead signature of landholder agreements. The role will also play a key role in ensuring compliance (contracts and carbon standards) as well as coordinate schedules between landholders and contractors for the implementation of reforestation activities. This will include confirming site readiness, conducting periodic field quality audits, documenting and tracking progress, and resolving issues that could delay delivery or degrade quality.  The role requires a strong combination stakeholder engagement and management experience, and a commitment to quality and impact. The role requires extensive travel and field work across Minas Gerais, Bahia and Espírito Santo.  Primary roles and responsibilities include:   Landholder engagement, onboarding, and pipeline management   Map priority municipalities and referral partner networks (city governments, co-ops, farmer associations, NGOs); plan and run outreach activities, events and information sessions.  Manage the landholder onboarding process (identify → qualify → onboard → contract), using CRM/trackers to keep status, documents and next actions current.  Prepare clear information packs (benefits, obligations, timelines) and respond to inquiries in a timely, professional manner.  Maintain ongoing landholder relationship management to support retention, satisfaction, and smooth site access throughout implementation.    Eligibility, due diligence & agreements   Coordinate site inspections and initial diagnostics in consultation with other team members (parcel boundaries, vegetation status, access, water, risks).  Support land tenure verification and FPIC documentation  Lead closure of contract signatures.  Maintain organized repository of all landholder records within Nature Co’s data management system   (land titles, eligibility documents, contracts, site maps, inspection notes, photos, consultation records).  Reforestation delivery enablement   Translate signed landholder agreements into implementation-ready site plans (site-specific scope, access instructions, constraints, schedule windows).  Align field schedules with landholders and contractors to ensure access, minimize disruption to farm activities, and maintain trust and cooperation.  Support in the delivery of field delivery progress from contractors by site (start/finish dates, activities completed, challenges, next steps), and escalate issues early (access, weather delays, input shortages, labor constraints).  Support in monitoring reforestation activities (during and post planting) and coordinate, where required, rapid response with contractors/landholders (grazing, fire risk, pests, drought stress).    Stakeholder engagement and safeguards   Plan and document stakeholder consultations and community meetings in accordance with Nature Co policies and procedures (agendas, attendance lists, minutes, photos).  Support the team in the operation of the grievance mechanism: receiving grievances and responding in accordance with the Nature Co grievance mechanism.  Maintain landholder contact and ensure landholder information is kept up to date.  Coordinate access, for other project staff and contractors as required.    Reporting   Lead or assist the development of formal monthly, quarterly, and annual project implementation reports for internal and external stakeholders in line with contract and/or carbon standard requirements.  Prepare ad hoc reports, documents, and presentations for internal and external stakeholders.    Teamwork and culture   Support the management of a cross-functional, international team, fostering collaboration and ensuring that project milestones and goals are met.  Stay current on emerging best practices in Nb S and carbon projects; proactively share insights across the organisation and with partners.    Skills and attributes   To perform successfully in this role, you will have:  A minimum of five (5) years of experience in reforestation projects with direct contact with rural landholders and reforestation planting service providers.  Degree in forest engineering, agronomy, ecology, or environmental science.  Intermediate English and native Portuguese language skills  Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to engage confidently across cultures and stakeholder groups.  Strong project management skills, including experience managing timelines, deliverables, and working across multidisciplinary teams.  A proactive, self-starting approach with the ability to anticipate problems, adapt quickly, and take initiative under limited supervision.  A collaborative mindset and ability to lead and motivate internal teams and external partners  Ability to provide strategic and technical guidance across complex, multi-stakeholder projects.  Strong organisational skills and attention to detail in documentation and reporting.  A positive, energetic personality with resilience and drive to see projects through to delivery.    Extensive travel within Brazil is a requirement to perform this position.   Location    Remote, with residence in Minas Gerais, Espirito Santo, or Bahia    Submission instructions   Email CV and brief cover letter to with subject: Landholder and Reforestation Delivery Manager  Submission deadline: 30 March 2026

title: Landholder and reforestation delivery manager
description:
Empresa está contratando Landholder and reforestation delivery manager em mogi das cruzes. Confira requisitos e envie seu currículo.

About Nature Co  Nature Co delivers nature-based solutions (Nb S) for investors, corporates and other purpose driven organisations to scale up action on climate change and biodiversity loss. We specialise in nature-based project development including reforestation, agroforestry, farmer managed natural regeneration and mangrove restoration. Nature Co has extensive expertise in working with local communities to protect and restore natural ecosystems through participation in the global voluntary carbon market.  Nature Co is currently implementing a large-scale reforestation project in Brazil for the generation of verified carbon credits.  We are a diverse, mission-driven team that values inclusion, integrity, and innovation. Nature Co is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer, committed to building an equitable and inclusive workplace for all.     Role and responsibilities   The Landholder and Reforestation Delivery Manager is the primary field-based interface with landholders, communities, reforestation contractors, and other local stakeholders for Nature Co’s projects in Brazil. This position will build and manage a pipeline of landholders interested in reforestation, lead outreach and onboarding, coordinate site inspections, lead the collection of relevant data required for carbon standard checks, and lead signature of landholder agreements. The role will also play a key role in ensuring compliance (contracts and carbon standards) as well as coordinate schedules between landholders and contractors for the implementation of reforestation activities. This will include confirming site readiness, conducting periodic field quality audits, documenting and tracking progress, and resolving issues that could delay delivery or degrade quality.  The role requires a strong combination stakeholder engagement and management experience, and a commitment to quality and impact. The role requires extensive travel and field work across Minas Gerais, Bahia and Espírito Santo.  Primary roles and responsibilities include:   Landholder engagement, onboarding, and pipeline management   Map priority municipalities and referral partner networks (city governments, co-ops, farmer associations, NGOs); plan and run outreach activities, events and information sessions.  Manage the landholder onboarding process (identify → qualify → onboard → contract), using CRM/trackers to keep status, documents and next actions current.  Prepare clear information packs (benefits, obligations, timelines) and respond to inquiries in a timely, professional manner.  Maintain ongoing landholder relationship management to support retention, satisfaction, and smooth site access throughout implementation.    Eligibility, due diligence & agreements   Coordinate site inspections and initial diagnostics in consultation with other team members (parcel boundaries, vegetation status, access, water, risks).  Support land tenure verification and FPIC documentation  Lead closure of contract signatures.  Maintain organized repository of all landholder records within Nature Co’s data management system   (land titles, eligibility documents, contracts, site maps, inspection notes, photos, consultation records).  Reforestation delivery enablement   Translate signed landholder agreements into implementation-ready site plans (site-specific scope, access instructions, constraints, schedule windows).  Align field schedules with landholders and contractors to ensure access, minimize disruption to farm activities, and maintain trust and cooperation.  Support in the delivery of field delivery progress from contractors by site (start/finish dates, activities completed, challenges, next steps), and escalate issues early (access, weather delays, input shortages, labor constraints).  Support in monitoring reforestation activities (during and post planting) and coordinate, where required, rapid response with contractors/landholders (grazing, fire risk, pests, drought stress).    Stakeholder engagement and safeguards   Plan and document stakeholder consultations and community meetings in accordance with Nature Co policies and procedures (agendas, attendance lists, minutes, photos).  Support the team in the operation of the grievance mechanism: receiving grievances and responding in accordance with the Nature Co grievance mechanism.  Maintain landholder contact and ensure landholder information is kept up to date.  Coordinate access, for other project staff and contractors as required.    Reporting   Lead or assist the development of formal monthly, quarterly, and annual project implementation reports for internal and external stakeholders in line with contract and/or carbon standard requirements.  Prepare ad hoc reports, documents, and presentations for internal and external stakeholders.    Teamwork and culture   Support the management of a cross-functional, international team, fostering collaboration and ensuring that project milestones and goals are met.  Stay current on emerging best practices in Nb S and carbon projects; proactively share insights across the organisation and with partners.    Skills and attributes   To perform successfully in this role, you will have:  A minimum of five (5) years of experience in reforestation projects with direct contact with rural landholders and reforestation planting service providers.  Degree in forest engineering, agronomy, ecology, or environmental science.  Intermediate English and native Portuguese language skills  Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to engage confidently across cultures and stakeholder groups.  Strong project management skills, including experience managing timelines, deliverables, and working across multidisciplinary teams.  A proactive, self-starting approach with the ability to anticipate problems, adapt quickly, and take initiative under limited supervision.  A collaborative mindset and ability to lead and motivate internal teams and external partners  Ability to provide strategic and technical guidance across complex, multi-stakeholder projects.  Strong organisational skills and attention to detail in documentation and reporting.  A positive, energetic personality with resilience and drive to see projects through to delivery.    Extensive travel within Brazil is a requirement to perform this position.   Location    Remote, with residence in Minas Gerais, Espirito Santo, or Bahia    Submission instructions   Email CV and brief cover letter to with subject: Landholder and Reforestation Delivery Manager  Submission deadline: 30 March 2026

title: Risk management officer
description:
Confira a vaga para Risk management officer em presidente prudente. Veja os detalhes e como se candidatar.

About Us  Established in March 2018, Bybit is one of the fastest growing cryptocurrency derivatives exchanges, with more than 70 million registered users. We offer a professional platform where crypto traders can find an ultra-fast matching engine, excellent customer service and multilingual community support. We provide innovative online spot and derivatives trading services, mining and staking products, as well as API support, to retail and institutional clients around the world, and strive to be the most reliable exchange for the emerging digital asset class.  Our core values define us. We listen, care, and improve to create a faster, fairer, and more humane trading environment for our users. Our innovative, highly advanced, user-friendly platform has been designed from the ground-up using best-in-class infrastructure to provide our users with the industry's safest, fastest, fairest, and most transparent trading experience. Built on customer-centric values, we endeavour to provide a professional, 24/7 multi-language customer support to help in a timely manner.  As of today, Bybit is one of the most trusted, reliable, and transparent cryptocurrency derivatives platforms in the space.  Key Responsibilities:   Implement and maintain a comprehensive risk management framework, covering credit, market, liquidity, operational, and technology risks.  Conduct prudential and capital risk assessments, including stress testing, scenario analysis, and capital adequacy evaluations.  Prepare and support regulatory disclosures required for virtual asset service providers (VASPs) and financial institutions.  Oversee Margin-Account Operations, including;  Development of policies governing margin lending and virtual asset collateral  Setting and reviewing maximum loan-to-value (LTV) ratios and haircut levels  Monitoring collateral valuation, capital add-ons and counterparty exposures  Ensuring compliance with client/institutional limits and capital requirements  Net-worth monitoring;  Review and monitor risk indicators across business functions, escalating material breaches or deviations to senior management and the Board.  Maintain independence from commercial and trading lines while ensuring collaboration with Compliance, Finance, and Operations.  Liaise with internal and external auditors, regulators, and governance committees on risk management and capital matters.  Support a risk-aware culture through training, communication, and continuous improvement of risk methodologies.  Deep practical knowledge in CMN Res. 4557/17 regarding the risk management structure, the financial structure and the information disclosure policy management.    Requirements:   Legally resident in Brazil.  Senior-level experience (minimum 7 years) in financial or prudential risk management, preferably within financial institutions, fintechs, or crypto/virtual asset firms.  Demonstrated  independence from commercial functions  and ability to operate as a second-line or independent control function.   Strong knowledge of  Central Bank of Brazil  risk management regulations, capital adequacy standards, and VASP disclosure requirements.   Expertise in market and liquidity risk frameworks, stress testing, and margin-account operations involving virtual assets.  Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Economics, Risk Management, or related field; postgraduate qualification preferred.  Strong quantitative, analytical, and communication skills; fluency in  Portuguese and English  .   Must meet  fit and proper  standards with  no disqualifying factors  , including:   not to have been declared bankrupt or insolvent;  unblemished reputation;  knowledge of the line of business, the services to be provided and the crypto segment, as well as crypto market dynamics and the risks associated with those activities;  technical capability, compatible with the functions to be exercised.  not having been previously rejected or investigated by the Central Bank of Brazil within the past three years for submitting false, omitted, or inconsistent information in any authorization request

Job Title: Salesforce Business Systems Analyst (BSA)  Location: LATAM   Duration: 6-12months   Job Summary:   We are looking for a  Salesforce Business Systems Analyst (BSA) with strong experience in gathering business requirements, translating them into functional specifications, and supporting Salesforce implementation and enhancements. title: Landholder and reforestation delivery manager
description:
Nova oportunidade para Landholder and reforestation delivery manager em cajamar. Saiba mais sobre essa vaga.

About Nature Co  Nature Co delivers nature-based solutions (Nb S) for investors, corporates and other purpose driven organisations to scale up action on climate change and biodiversity loss. We specialise in nature-based project development including reforestation, agroforestry, farmer managed natural regeneration and mangrove restoration. Nature Co has extensive expertise in working with local communities to protect and restore natural ecosystems through participation in the global voluntary carbon market.  Nature Co is currently implementing a large-scale reforestation project in Brazil for the generation of verified carbon credits.  We are a diverse, mission-driven team that values inclusion, integrity, and innovation. Nature Co is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer, committed to building an equitable and inclusive workplace for all.     Role and responsibilities   The Landholder and Reforestation Delivery Manager is the primary field-based interface with landholders, communities, reforestation contractors, and other local stakeholders for Nature Co’s projects in Brazil. This position will build and manage a pipeline of landholders interested in reforestation, lead outreach and onboarding, coordinate site inspections, lead the collection of relevant data required for carbon standard checks, and lead signature of landholder agreements. The role will also play a key role in ensuring compliance (contracts and carbon standards) as well as coordinate schedules between landholders and contractors for the implementation of reforestation activities. This will include confirming site readiness, conducting periodic field quality audits, documenting and tracking progress, and resolving issues that could delay delivery or degrade quality.  The role requires a strong combination stakeholder engagement and management experience, and a commitment to quality and impact. The role requires extensive travel and field work across Minas Gerais, Bahia and Espírito Santo.  Primary roles and responsibilities include:   Landholder engagement, onboarding, and pipeline management   Map priority municipalities and referral partner networks (city governments, co-ops, farmer associations, NGOs); plan and run outreach activities, events and information sessions.  Manage the landholder onboarding process (identify → qualify → onboard → contract), using CRM/trackers to keep status, documents and next actions current.  Prepare clear information packs (benefits, obligations, timelines) and respond to inquiries in a timely, professional manner.  Maintain ongoing landholder relationship management to support retention, satisfaction, and smooth site access throughout implementation.    Eligibility, due diligence & agreements   Coordinate site inspections and initial diagnostics in consultation with other team members (parcel boundaries, vegetation status, access, water, risks).  Support land tenure verification and FPIC documentation  Lead closure of contract signatures.  Maintain organized repository of all landholder records within Nature Co’s data management system   (land titles, eligibility documents, contracts, site maps, inspection notes, photos, consultation records).  Reforestation delivery enablement   Translate signed landholder agreements into implementation-ready site plans (site-specific scope, access instructions, constraints, schedule windows).  Align field schedules with landholders and contractors to ensure access, minimize disruption to farm activities, and maintain trust and cooperation.  Support in the delivery of field delivery progress from contractors by site (start/finish dates, activities completed, challenges, next steps), and escalate issues early (access, weather delays, input shortages, labor constraints).  Support in monitoring reforestation activities (during and post planting) and coordinate, where required, rapid response with contractors/landholders (grazing, fire risk, pests, drought stress).    Stakeholder engagement and safeguards   Plan and document stakeholder consultations and community meetings in accordance with Nature Co policies and procedures (agendas, attendance lists, minutes, photos).  Support the team in the operation of the grievance mechanism: receiving grievances and responding in accordance with the Nature Co grievance mechanism.  Maintain landholder contact and ensure landholder information is kept up to date.  Coordinate access, for other project staff and contractors as required.    Reporting   Lead or assist the development of formal monthly, quarterly, and annual project implementation reports for internal and external stakeholders in line with contract and/or carbon standard requirements.  Prepare ad hoc reports, documents, and presentations for internal and external stakeholders.    Teamwork and culture   Support the management of a cross-functional, international team, fostering collaboration and ensuring that project milestones and goals are met.  Stay current on emerging best practices in Nb S and carbon projects; proactively share insights across the organisation and with partners.    Skills and attributes   To perform successfully in this role, you will have:  A minimum of five (5) years of experience in reforestation projects with direct contact with rural landholders and reforestation planting service providers.  Degree in forest engineering, agronomy, ecology, or environmental science.  Intermediate English and native Portuguese language skills  Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to engage confidently across cultures and stakeholder groups.  Strong project management skills, including experience managing timelines, deliverables, and working across multidisciplinary teams.  A proactive, self-starting approach with the ability to anticipate problems, adapt quickly, and take initiative under limited supervision.  A collaborative mindset and ability to lead and motivate internal teams and external partners  Ability to provide strategic and technical guidance across complex, multi-stakeholder projects.  Strong organisational skills and attention to detail in documentation and reporting.  A positive, energetic personality with resilience and drive to see projects through to delivery.    Extensive travel within Brazil is a requirement to perform this position.   Location    Remote, with residence in Minas Gerais, Espirito Santo, or Bahia    Submission instructions   Email CV and brief cover letter to with subject: Landholder and Reforestation Delivery Manager  Submission deadline: 30 March 2026

title: Landholder and reforestation delivery manager
description:
Empresa está contratando Landholder and reforestation delivery manager em caieiras. Confira requisitos e envie seu currículo.

About Nature Co  Nature Co delivers nature-based solutions (Nb S) for investors, corporates and other purpose driven organisations to scale up action on climate change and biodiversity loss. We specialise in nature-based project development including reforestation, agroforestry, farmer managed natural regeneration and mangrove restoration. Nature Co has extensive expertise in working with local communities to protect and restore natural ecosystems through participation in the global voluntary carbon market.  Nature Co is currently implementing a large-scale reforestation project in Brazil for the generation of verified carbon credits.  We are a diverse, mission-driven team that values inclusion, integrity, and innovation. Nature Co is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer, committed to building an equitable and inclusive workplace for all.     Role and responsibilities   The Landholder and Reforestation Delivery Manager is the primary field-based interface with landholders, communities, reforestation contractors, and other local stakeholders for Nature Co’s projects in Brazil. This position will build and manage a pipeline of landholders interested in reforestation, lead outreach and onboarding, coordinate site inspections, lead the collection of relevant data required for carbon standard checks, and lead signature of landholder agreements. The role will also play a key role in ensuring compliance (contracts and carbon standards) as well as coordinate schedules between landholders and contractors for the implementation of reforestation activities. This will include confirming site readiness, conducting periodic field quality audits, documenting and tracking progress, and resolving issues that could delay delivery or degrade quality.  The role requires a strong combination stakeholder engagement and management experience, and a commitment to quality and impact. The role requires extensive travel and field work across Minas Gerais, Bahia and Espírito Santo.  Primary roles and responsibilities include:   Landholder engagement, onboarding, and pipeline management   Map priority municipalities and referral partner networks (city governments, co-ops, farmer associations, NGOs); plan and run outreach activities, events and information sessions.  Manage the landholder onboarding process (identify → qualify → onboard → contract), using CRM/trackers to keep status, documents and next actions current.  Prepare clear information packs (benefits, obligations, timelines) and respond to inquiries in a timely, professional manner.  Maintain ongoing landholder relationship management to support retention, satisfaction, and smooth site access throughout implementation.    Eligibility, due diligence & agreements   Coordinate site inspections and initial diagnostics in consultation with other team members (parcel boundaries, vegetation status, access, water, risks).  Support land tenure verification and FPIC documentation  Lead closure of contract signatures.  Maintain organized repository of all landholder records within Nature Co’s data management system   (land titles, eligibility documents, contracts, site maps, inspection notes, photos, consultation records).  Reforestation delivery enablement   Translate signed landholder agreements into implementation-ready site plans (site-specific scope, access instructions, constraints, schedule windows).  Align field schedules with landholders and contractors to ensure access, minimize disruption to farm activities, and maintain trust and cooperation.  Support in the delivery of field delivery progress from contractors by site (start/finish dates, activities completed, challenges, next steps), and escalate issues early (access, weather delays, input shortages, labor constraints).  Support in monitoring reforestation activities (during and post planting) and coordinate, where required, rapid response with contractors/landholders (grazing, fire risk, pests, drought stress).    Stakeholder engagement and safeguards   Plan and document stakeholder consultations and community meetings in accordance with Nature Co policies and procedures (agendas, attendance lists, minutes, photos).  Support the team in the operation of the grievance mechanism: receiving grievances and responding in accordance with the Nature Co grievance mechanism.  Maintain landholder contact and ensure landholder information is kept up to date.  Coordinate access, for other project staff and contractors as required.    Reporting   Lead or assist the development of formal monthly, quarterly, and annual project implementation reports for internal and external stakeholders in line with contract and/or carbon standard requirements.  Prepare ad hoc reports, documents, and presentations for internal and external stakeholders.    Teamwork and culture   Support the management of a cross-functional, international team, fostering collaboration and ensuring that project milestones and goals are met.  Stay current on emerging best practices in Nb S and carbon projects; proactively share insights across the organisation and with partners.    Skills and attributes   To perform successfully in this role, you will have:  A minimum of five (5) years of experience in reforestation projects with direct contact with rural landholders and reforestation planting service providers.  Degree in forest engineering, agronomy, ecology, or environmental science.  Intermediate English and native Portuguese language skills  Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to engage confidently across cultures and stakeholder groups.  Strong project management skills, including experience managing timelines, deliverables, and working across multidisciplinary teams.  A proactive, self-starting approach with the ability to anticipate problems, adapt quickly, and take initiative under limited supervision.  A collaborative mindset and ability to lead and motivate internal teams and external partners  Ability to provide strategic and technical guidance across complex, multi-stakeholder projects.  Strong organisational skills and attention to detail in documentation and reporting.  A positive, energetic personality with resilience and drive to see projects through to delivery. title: Landholder and reforestation delivery manager
description:
Empresa está contratando Landholder and reforestation delivery manager em araucária. Confira requisitos e envie seu currículo.

About Nature Co  Nature Co delivers nature-based solutions (Nb S) for investors, corporates and other purpose driven organisations to scale up action on climate change and biodiversity loss. We specialise in nature-based project development including reforestation, agroforestry, farmer managed natural regeneration and mangrove restoration. Nature Co has extensive expertise in working with local communities to protect and restore natural ecosystems through participation in the global voluntary carbon market.  Nature Co is currently implementing a large-scale reforestation project in Brazil for the generation of verified carbon credits.  We are a diverse, mission-driven team that values inclusion, integrity, and innovation. Nature Co is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer, committed to building an equitable and inclusive workplace for all.     Role and responsibilities   The Landholder and Reforestation Delivery Manager is the primary field-based interface with landholders, communities, reforestation contractors, and other local stakeholders for Nature Co’s projects in Brazil. This position will build and manage a pipeline of landholders interested in reforestation, lead outreach and onboarding, coordinate site inspections, lead the collection of relevant data required for carbon standard checks, and lead signature of landholder agreements. The role will also play a key role in ensuring compliance (contracts and carbon standards) as well as coordinate schedules between landholders and contractors for the implementation of reforestation activities. This will include confirming site readiness, conducting periodic field quality audits, documenting and tracking progress, and resolving issues that could delay delivery or degrade quality.  The role requires a strong combination stakeholder engagement and management experience, and a commitment to quality and impact. The role requires extensive travel and field work across Minas Gerais, Bahia and Espírito Santo.  Primary roles and responsibilities include:   Landholder engagement, onboarding, and pipeline management   Map priority municipalities and referral partner networks (city governments, co-ops, farmer associations, NGOs); plan and run outreach activities, events and information sessions.  Manage the landholder onboarding process (identify → qualify → onboard → contract), using CRM/trackers to keep status, documents and next actions current.  Prepare clear information packs (benefits, obligations, timelines) and respond to inquiries in a timely, professional manner.  Maintain ongoing landholder relationship management to support retention, satisfaction, and smooth site access throughout implementation.    Eligibility, due diligence & agreements   Coordinate site inspections and initial diagnostics in consultation with other team members (parcel boundaries, vegetation status, access, water, risks).  Support land tenure verification and FPIC documentation  Lead closure of contract signatures.  Maintain organized repository of all landholder records within Nature Co’s data management system   (land titles, eligibility documents, contracts, site maps, inspection notes, photos, consultation records).  Reforestation delivery enablement   Translate signed landholder agreements into implementation-ready site plans (site-specific scope, access instructions, constraints, schedule windows).  Align field schedules with landholders and contractors to ensure access, minimize disruption to farm activities, and maintain trust and cooperation.  Support in the delivery of field delivery progress from contractors by site (start/finish dates, activities completed, challenges, next steps), and escalate issues early (access, weather delays, input shortages, labor constraints).  Support in monitoring reforestation activities (during and post planting) and coordinate, where required, rapid response with contractors/landholders (grazing, fire risk, pests, drought stress).    Stakeholder engagement and safeguards   Plan and document stakeholder consultations and community meetings in accordance with Nature Co policies and procedures (agendas, attendance lists, minutes, photos).  Support the team in the operation of the grievance mechanism: receiving grievances and responding in accordance with the Nature Co grievance mechanism.  Maintain landholder contact and ensure landholder information is kept up to date.  Coordinate access, for other project staff and contractors as required.    Reporting   Lead or assist the development of formal monthly, quarterly, and annual project implementation reports for internal and external stakeholders in line with contract and/or carbon standard requirements.  Prepare ad hoc reports, documents, and presentations for internal and external stakeholders.    Teamwork and culture   Support the management of a cross-functional, international team, fostering collaboration and ensuring that project milestones and goals are met.  Stay current on emerging best practices in Nb S and carbon projects; proactively share insights across the organisation and with partners.    Skills and attributes   To perform successfully in this role, you will have:  A minimum of five (5) years of experience in reforestation projects with direct contact with rural landholders and reforestation planting service providers.  Degree in forest engineering, agronomy, ecology, or environmental science.  Intermediate English and native Portuguese language skills  Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to engage confidently across cultures and stakeholder groups.  Strong project management skills, including experience managing timelines, deliverables, and working across multidisciplinary teams.  A proactive, self-starting approach with the ability to anticipate problems, adapt quickly, and take initiative under limited supervision.  A collaborative mindset and ability to lead and motivate internal teams and external partners  Ability to provide strategic and technical guidance across complex, multi-stakeholder projects.  Strong organisational skills and attention to detail in documentation and reporting.  A positive, energetic personality with resilience and drive to see projects through to delivery.    Extensive travel within Brazil is a requirement to perform this position.   Location    Remote, with residence in Minas Gerais, Espirito Santo, or Bahia    Submission instructions   Email CV and brief cover letter to with subject: Landholder and Reforestation Delivery Manager  Submission deadline: 30 March 2026

title: Landholder and reforestation delivery manager
description:
Nova oportunidade para Landholder and reforestation delivery manager em guarujá. Saiba mais sobre essa vaga.

About Nature Co  Nature Co delivers nature-based solutions (Nb S) for investors, corporates and other purpose driven organisations to scale up action on climate change and biodiversity loss. We specialise in nature-based project development including reforestation, agroforestry, farmer managed natural regeneration and mangrove restoration. Nature Co has extensive expertise in working with local communities to protect and restore natural ecosystems through participation in the global voluntary carbon market.  Nature Co is currently implementing a large-scale reforestation project in Brazil for the generation of verified carbon credits.  We are a diverse, mission-driven team that values inclusion, integrity, and innovation. Nature Co is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer, committed to building an equitable and inclusive workplace for all.     Role and responsibilities   The Landholder and Reforestation Delivery Manager is the primary field-based interface with landholders, communities, reforestation contractors, and other local stakeholders for Nature Co’s projects in Brazil. This position will build and manage a pipeline of landholders interested in reforestation, lead outreach and onboarding, coordinate site inspections, lead the collection of relevant data required for carbon standard checks, and lead signature of landholder agreements. The role will also play a key role in ensuring compliance (contracts and carbon standards) as well as coordinate schedules between landholders and contractors for the implementation of reforestation activities. This will include confirming site readiness, conducting periodic field quality audits, documenting and tracking progress, and resolving issues that could delay delivery or degrade quality.  The role requires a strong combination stakeholder engagement and management experience, and a commitment to quality and impact. The role requires extensive travel and field work across Minas Gerais, Bahia and Espírito Santo.  Primary roles and responsibilities include:   Landholder engagement, onboarding, and pipeline management   Map priority municipalities and referral partner networks (city governments, co-ops, farmer associations, NGOs); plan and run outreach activities, events and information sessions.  Manage the landholder onboarding process (identify → qualify → onboard → contract), using CRM/trackers to keep status, documents and next actions current.  Prepare clear information packs (benefits, obligations, timelines) and respond to inquiries in a timely, professional manner.  Maintain ongoing landholder relationship management to support retention, satisfaction, and smooth site access throughout implementation.    Eligibility, due diligence & agreements   Coordinate site inspections and initial diagnostics in consultation with other team members (parcel boundaries, vegetation status, access, water, risks).  Support land tenure verification and FPIC documentation  Lead closure of contract signatures.  Maintain organized repository of all landholder records within Nature Co’s data management system   (land titles, eligibility documents, contracts, site maps, inspection notes, photos, consultation records).  Reforestation delivery enablement   Translate signed landholder agreements into implementation-ready site plans (site-specific scope, access instructions, constraints, schedule windows).  Align field schedules with landholders and contractors to ensure access, minimize disruption to farm activities, and maintain trust and cooperation.  Support in the delivery of field delivery progress from contractors by site (start/finish dates, activities completed, challenges, next steps), and escalate issues early (access, weather delays, input shortages, labor constraints).  Support in monitoring reforestation activities (during and post planting) and coordinate, where required, rapid response with contractors/landholders (grazing, fire risk, pests, drought stress).    Stakeholder engagement and safeguards   Plan and document stakeholder consultations and community meetings in accordance with Nature Co policies and procedures (agendas, attendance lists, minutes, photos).  Support the team in the operation of the grievance mechanism: receiving grievances and responding in accordance with the Nature Co grievance mechanism.  Maintain landholder contact and ensure landholder information is kept up to date.  Coordinate access, for other project staff and contractors as required.    Reporting   Lead or assist the development of formal monthly, quarterly, and annual project implementation reports for internal and external stakeholders in line with contract and/or carbon standard requirements.  Prepare ad hoc reports, documents, and presentations for internal and external stakeholders.    Teamwork and culture   Support the management of a cross-functional, international team, fostering collaboration and ensuring that project milestones and goals are met.  Stay current on emerging best practices in Nb S and carbon projects; proactively share insights across the organisation and with partners.    Skills and attributes   To perform successfully in this role, you will have:  A minimum of five (5) years of experience in reforestation projects with direct contact with rural landholders and reforestation planting service providers.  Degree in forest engineering, agronomy, ecology, or environmental science.  Intermediate English and native Portuguese language skills  Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to engage confidently across cultures and stakeholder groups.  Strong project management skills, including experience managing timelines, deliverables, and working across multidisciplinary teams.  A proactive, self-starting approach with the ability to anticipate problems, adapt quickly, and take initiative under limited supervision.  A collaborative mindset and ability to lead and motivate internal teams and external partners  Ability to provide strategic and technical guidance across complex, multi-stakeholder projects.  Strong organisational skills and attention to detail in documentation and reporting.  A positive, energetic personality with resilience and drive to see projects through to delivery.    Extensive travel within Brazil is a requirement to perform this position.   Location    Remote, with residence in Minas Gerais, Espirito Santo, or Bahia    Submission instructions   Email CV and brief cover letter to with subject: Landholder and Reforestation Delivery Manager  Submission deadline: 30 March 2026

title: Landholder and reforestation delivery manager
description:
Confira a vaga para Landholder and reforestation delivery manager em presidente prudente. Veja os detalhes e como se candidatar.

About Nature Co  Nature Co delivers nature-based solutions (Nb S) for investors, corporates and other purpose driven organisations to scale up action on climate change and biodiversity loss. We specialise in nature-based project development including reforestation, agroforestry, farmer managed natural regeneration and mangrove restoration. Nature Co has extensive expertise in working with local communities to protect and restore natural ecosystems through participation in the global voluntary carbon market.  Nature Co is currently implementing a large-scale reforestation project in Brazil for the generation of verified carbon credits.  We are a diverse, mission-driven team that values inclusion, integrity, and innovation. Nature Co is proud to be an Equal Opportunity Employer, committed to building an equitable and inclusive workplace for all.     Role and responsibilities   The Landholder and Reforestation Delivery Manager is the primary field-based interface with landholders, communities, reforestation contractors, and other local stakeholders for Nature Co’s projects in Brazil. This position will build and manage a pipeline of landholders interested in reforestation, lead outreach and onboarding, coordinate site inspections, lead the collection of relevant data required for carbon standard checks, and lead signature of landholder agreements. The role will also play a key role in ensuring compliance (contracts and carbon standards) as well as coordinate schedules between landholders and contractors for the implementation of reforestation activities. This will include confirming site readiness, conducting periodic field quality audits, documenting and tracking progress, and resolving issues that could delay delivery or degrade quality.  The role requires a strong combination stakeholder engagement and management experience, and a commitment to quality and impact. The role requires extensive travel and field work across Minas Gerais, Bahia and Espírito Santo.  Primary roles and responsibilities include:   Landholder engagement, onboarding, and pipeline management   Map priority municipalities and referral partner networks (city governments, co-ops, farmer associations, NGOs); plan and run outreach activities, events and information sessions.  Manage the landholder onboarding process (identify → qualify → onboard → contract), using CRM/trackers to keep status, documents and next actions current.  Prepare clear information packs (benefits, obligations, timelines) and respond to inquiries in a timely, professional manner.  Maintain ongoing landholder relationship management to support retention, satisfaction, and smooth site access throughout implementation.    Eligibility, due diligence & agreements   Coordinate site inspections and initial diagnostics in consultation with other team members (parcel boundaries, vegetation status, access, water, risks).  Support land tenure verification and FPIC documentation  Lead closure of contract signatures.  Maintain organized repository of all landholder records within Nature Co’s data management system   (land titles, eligibility documents, contracts, site maps, inspection notes, photos, consultation records).  Reforestation delivery enablement   Translate signed landholder agreements into implementation-ready site plans (site-specific scope, access instructions, constraints, schedule windows).  Align field schedules with landholders and contractors to ensure access, minimize disruption to farm activities, and maintain trust and cooperation.  Support in the delivery of field delivery progress from contractors by site (start/finish dates, activities completed, challenges, next steps), and escalate issues early (access, weather delays, input shortages, labor constraints).  Support in monitoring reforestation activities (during and post planting) and coordinate, where required, rapid response with contractors/landholders (grazing, fire risk, pests, drought stress).    Stakeholder engagement and safeguards   Plan and document stakeholder consultations and community meetings in accordance with Nature Co policies and procedures (agendas, attendance lists, minutes, photos).  Support the team in the operation of the grievance mechanism: receiving grievances and responding in accordance with the Nature Co grievance mechanism.  Maintain landholder contact and ensure landholder information is kept up to date.  Coordinate access, for other project staff and contractors as required.    Reporting   Lead or assist the development of formal monthly, quarterly, and annual project implementation reports for internal and external stakeholders in line with contract and/or carbon standard requirements.  Prepare ad hoc reports, documents, and presentations for internal and external stakeholders.    Teamwork and culture   Support the management of a cross-functional, international team, fostering collaboration and ensuring that project milestones and goals are met.  Stay current on emerging best practices in Nb S and carbon projects; proactively share insights across the organisation and with partners.    Skills and attributes   To perform successfully in this role, you will have:  A minimum of five (5) years of experience in reforestation projects with direct contact with rural landholders and reforestation planting service providers.  Degree in forest engineering, agronomy, ecology, or environmental science.  Intermediate English and native Portuguese language skills  Excellent written and verbal communication skills, with the ability to engage confidently across cultures and stakeholder groups.  Strong project management skills, including experience managing timelines, deliverables, and working across multidisciplinary teams.  A proactive, self-starting approach with the ability to anticipate problems, adapt quickly, and take initiative under limited supervision.  A collaborative mindset and ability to lead and motivate internal teams and external partners  Ability to provide strategic and technical guidance across complex, multi-stakeholder projects.  Strong organisational skills and attention to detail in documentation and reporting.  A positive, energetic personality with resilience and drive to see projects through to delivery. As of today, Bybit is one of the most trusted, reliable, and transparent cryptocurrency derivatives platforms in the space.  Key Responsibilities:   Implement and maintain a comprehensive risk management framework, covering credit, market, liquidity, operational, and technology risks.  Conduct prudential and capital risk assessments, including stress testing, scenario analysis, and capital adequacy evaluations.  Prepare and support regulatory disclosures required for virtual asset service providers (VASPs) and financial institutions.  Oversee Margin-Account Operations, including;  Development of policies governing margin lending and virtual asset collateral  Setting and reviewing maximum loan-to-value (LTV) ratios and haircut levels  Monitoring collateral valuation, capital add-ons and counterparty exposures  Ensuring compliance with client/institutional limits and capital requirements  Net-worth monitoring;  Review and monitor risk indicators across business functions, escalating material breaches or deviations to senior management and the Board.  Maintain independence from commercial and trading lines while ensuring collaboration with Compliance, Finance, and Operations.  Liaise with internal and external auditors, regulators, and governance committees on risk management and capital matters.  Support a risk-aware culture through training, communication, and continuous improvement of risk methodologies.  Deep practical knowledge in CMN Res. 4557/17 regarding the risk management structure, the financial structure and the information disclosure policy management.    Requirements:   Legally resident in Brazil.  Senior-level experience (minimum 7 years) in financial or prudential risk management, preferably within financial institutions, fintechs, or crypto/virtual asset firms.  Demonstrated  independence from commercial functions  and ability to operate as a second-line or independent control function.   Strong knowledge of  Central Bank of Brazil  risk management regulations, capital adequacy standards, and VASP disclosure requirements.   Expertise in market and liquidity risk frameworks, stress testing, and margin-account operations involving virtual assets.  Bachelor’s degree in Finance, Economics, Risk Management, or related field; postgraduate qualification preferred.  Strong quantitative, analytical, and communication skills; fluency in  Portuguese and English  .   Must meet  fit and proper  standards with  no disqualifying factors  , including:   not to have been declared bankrupt or insolvent;  unblemished reputation;  knowledge of the line of business, the services to be provided and the crypto segment, as well as crypto market dynamics and the risks associated with those activities;  technical capability, compatible with the functions to be exercised.  not having been previously rejected or investigated by the Central Bank of Brazil within the past three years for submitting false, omitted, or inconsistent information in any authorization request

title: Web3 & al investment analyst
description:
Confira a vaga para Web3 & al investment analyst em embu. Veja os detalhes e como se candidatar.

Web3 DXB  is a Dubai-based investment and research platform focused on identifying and scaling high-potential opportunities at the intersection of  blockchain, artificial intelligence, and next-generation digital infrastructure  . We combine deep market insight with an agile, thesis-driven approach to back transformative technologies shaping the future of finance and the internet.  As we expand our investment activities, we are looking for a highly analytical and forward-thinking  Web3 & AI Investment Analyst  to join our team. This is a  fully remote position (Poland-based) , offering direct exposure to early-stage deals, market research, and high-impact investment decisions across Web3 and AI.  This role is ideal for someone who lives at the edge of innovation — tracking narratives, identifying asymmetric opportunities, and translating complex trends into actionable investment insights.   What You’ll Be Doing  Conduct deep-dive research on Web3 and AI sectors, including protocols, startups, and emerging technologies.  Analyze market trends, narratives, and macro developments across crypto and AI ecosystems.  Evaluate investment opportunities, including token projects, early-stage startups, and infrastructure plays.  Build investment theses and present insights to internal stakeholders.  Monitor portfolio performance and track key metrics across projects.  Collaborate with internal teams on strategy, deal flow, and market positioning.  Stay ahead of industry developments, identifying early signals and high-potential opportunities.     What We’re Looking For  2–4+ years of experience in investment analysis, research, venture capital, or crypto/AI markets.  Strong understanding of blockchain, De Fi, tokenomics, and Web3 ecosystems.  Solid knowledge or strong interest in artificial intelligence and its investment landscape.  Exceptional analytical and research skills with the ability to synthesize complex information.  Experience evaluating startups, token models, or market opportunities.  Ability to think independently and form high-conviction investment views.  Fluent English with strong written communication skills.  High level of curiosity, ownership, and performance orientation.     Why Join Web3 DXB  Competitive compensation:  BRL 560,000 – 770,000 + performance-based bonuses.   Remote-first:  Fully remote (Poland-based) with flexible working hours.   Direct investment exposure:  Work on real deals and high-impact decisions.   High-growth environment:  Operate at the intersection of Web3 and AI — two of the fastest-growing sectors globally.   Meritocratic culture:  Your ideas and insights directly influence outcomes.  Long-term upside:  Be part of a team shaping the future of decentralized and intelligent systems.    If you’re passionate about  Web3, AI, and investing  , and want to operate where innovation meets capital, we’d love to connect.

Syniti’s Data First strategy transforms data from an afterthought into a strategic asset—unlocking insights, reducing risk, and fueling growth. With over 5,000 successful projects, we support the full data lifecycle through a unified platform for migration, quality, replication, matching, master data management, analytics, governance, and strategy.  Operating globally across industries, Syniti’s award-winning software, expert consultants give enterprises a unique edge in managing and maximizing their data.  Syniti’s cloud-native platform sets new standards in enterprise data management, combining powerful Saa S solutions with deep domain expertise. Designed for agility and scale, our technology helps customers accelerate digital transformation, drive innovation, and make confident decisions with trusted data. Every product enhancement is built to solve real business challenges—empowering organizations to unlock value from their data faster and more effectively.  THE ROLE   We are seeking a highly technical and execution‑driven  Technical Product Owner  to serve as the “engine room” of our platform. In this role, you will translate high‑level product strategy into clear, actionable, and technically sound work for engineering teams. You will bridge complex legacy ERP architectures (SAP S/4 HANA, ECC) with modern, cloud‑native, AI‑driven workflows across the Syniti Knowledge Platform. This role goes far beyond writing tickets — we are looking for someone who uses AI for deep research, builds mockup screens to define user journeys, and ensures the creation of the “Golden Record” through seamless end‑to‑end integration across cataloging, migration, quality, and governance.  What You’ll Do   Product Ownership & Agile Execution: Lead 2–3 scrum teams by owning and prioritizing the backlog for key SKP capabilities (Migrate, Replicate, Drive, Orchestrate). Run high-impact backlog grooming, sprint planning, and estimation sessions.  Modern Requirement Engineering: Translate strategy into crisp Epics and User Stories. Use AI-driven tools to accelerate documentation, explore ERP integration patterns, and generate edge-case test scenarios.  UX & Workflow Prototyping: Design mockups and wireframes (Figma, v0, Miro) to visualize data journeys. Ensure that both Data Stewards and Developers experience intuitive, world‑class workflows within SKP.  Lifecycle Integration: Partner with Architecture and Engineering to define functional and non‑functional requirements (scalability, security). Ensure seamless integration across the entire data lifecycle to eliminate duplication and unlock full platform value.  Quality & Acceptance: Collaborate with the PXQ team to define “What Good Looks Like.” Act as the final validation gate to ensure features meet enterprise standards and align with real‑world user behavior.  Operational Feedback Loop: Engage with Support and Customer Success to funnel production learnings into the backlog, ensuring continuous improvement based on real customer usage.    WHAT IT TAKES   The Technical Veteran: 5+ years as a Product Owner or Business Analyst working on enterprise data products. Strong understanding of data integration, replication, APIs, and cloud-native architectures (AWS/Azure).  The ERP Expert: Deep experience with SAP ecosystems and large-scale transformation programs. Understanding of MDM, Data Quality, and Governance “plumbing.” Experience with SAP MDG or Informatica is a major plus.  The Modern Builder: An AI-native thinker who uses LLMs to enhance productivity and research. Prefers mockups over long documents and thrives in visual communication.  The Agile Leader: CSPO-certified with demonstrated ability to manage risks, dependencies, and scope changes across distributed, multi-time‑zone teams.  The Academic: Bachelor’s degree in Engineering, Computer Science, or related practical experience.  The Communicator: Able to clearly articulate complex data and replication logic to business users while also explaining product vision to engineering teams.    Key Skills    Visionary Leadership:  Ability to maintain a clear product vision, define objectives, and mentor teams toward business goals.   Advanced Governance Concepts:  Strong command of data management and governance principles, including hierarchy and survivorship rules.   AI/ML Application:  Experience using AI/ML tools for documentation automation, market trend analysis, and optimization of data‑matching or data‑cleansing logic.   Visual Communication:  Skilled at producing wireframes and process flows to ensure UX alignment.   Technical Storyboarding:  Ability to write precise user stories and acceptance criteria with zero ambiguity.   Relationship Orchestration:  Strong interpersonal skills to influence stakeholders and drive collaborative engagement.  Drive for Results:  Relentless focus on delivering incremental value and ensuring release readiness in a fast‑moving environment.    Be fully aligned with our core values:  Think Big  - Be courageous and bold. Aspire to greatness. Relentlessly pursue market innovation. Set the standard by which others follow. Create solutions that have a meaningful impact. Solve the challenges our customers don’t know they have.  Be Curious  - Be a lifelong learner. Seek out new ideas to serve customers. Understand our competition and the world. Be permanently dissatisfied with the status quo. Challenge preconceptions. Focus on the future rather than yesterday.  Take Action  - Be the first. Don’t wait. Take accountability. Inspire others by doing. Fail fast and learn from mistakes. Make a difference every day.  Stronger Together  - Respect, trust and look out for each other. Celebrate diverse perspectives. Listen. Build connections and belonging. Act with integrity. Give back. One Syniti family.  By applying for this position, you acknowledge and consent to your image being captured (video or screenshot) for employment purposes, including during the hiring and onboarding process.   WHAT WE OFFER   Trust that you are proficient at what you do. At Syniti, you will find a supportive environment and access to learning tools, but micromanagement is not our thing.  Growth. We are growing rapidly and steadily solving the biggest challenges enterprise companies are faced with today. There was never a better time to join and grow with us. Most importantly, you will have the chance to shape our journey and share in our success story.  Support. We all rely on each other and enable each other to be successful. You won’t stand alone.  Curiosity and genuine interest in you. We all have our different stories, all equally fascinating, with each depicting a different journey, and we want to hear them all.  Recognition. We are the sum of individual achievements, and we always take the time to celebrate them.  An open organisation. Hierarchies are not our thing, and access is something we make sure of across the board. We are a family where everyone is just as important, everyone’s work is seen, and ideas are valued.    OUR COMMITMENT TO INCLUSION  At Syniti, we’re committed to creating a respectful, inclusive, and fair workplace where everyone belongs and thrives. We believe that diverse perspectives make us stronger — and we value the unique backgrounds, experiences, and voices each person brings to our team.  We welcome applicants based on their skills and potential, and we’re dedicated to ensuring equal opportunities for all, regardless of personal background. If you need accommodations during the hiring process, please let us know — we’re here to support you.
